Q: How should an LLM judge be calibrated and protected against evaluation leakage?
A: A model judge implements a fallible measurement procedure. Define a rubric with concrete anchors, compare its judgments against qualified human review and inspect disagreement by important slice. The judge can be sensitive to wording, answer order, verbosity and adversarial instructions inside the evaluated content. Keep reference labels and held-out cases out of the tested system's tuning path. Version the judge model, prompt and parsing policy, and report uncertainty instead of treating an unexplained numeric score as objective truth.
Why: A verbose unsupported answer can receive a higher helpfulness score than a concise supported answer if the rubric rewards style indirectly. Human-reviewed counterexamples reveal the mismatch between the judge and the intended standard.
Risk: Optimizing directly against one judge can overfit its preferences.
Trade: Automated judges scale review but need calibration, sampling and explicit limitations.
Try: Blindly review judge disagreements and refine the rubric before using it as a release gate.
